background_texts:
Before the invasion, they lived an ordinary life, until ADVENT took everything from them. Their family disappeared during a mass roundup, leaving them with nothing but anger and a desperate need to survive.

For years, they fought the occupation from the shadows, sabotaging supply lines and ambushing patrols. They never stayed in one place long and trusted nobody easily. When an operation went wrong and their resistance cell was wiped out, they refused to abandon a wounded comrade, fighting until an XCOM extraction team arrived.

Impressed by their determination, XCOM offered them a place among its ranks. Now they fight not for glory or revenge, but for a future where nobody has to endure what they did. The aliens took their past. They won't let them take humanity's future.

Once a medic in an overcrowded refugee camp, they spent years trying to save lives while ADVENT's occupation made survival increasingly impossible. When soldiers stormed the camp and began executing suspected resistance sympathizers, they took up a weapon for the first time. They escaped with a handful of survivors, but the experience changed them forever. Now serving with XCOM, they carry medical supplies beside their rifle, determined to ensure that no one under their protection is left behind again.

Once a skilled mechanic, they spent the occupation repairing equipment for ADVENT, keeping their head down to avoid suspicion. Secretly, they sabotaged weapons and vehicles whenever they could. When their deception was discovered, they escaped with nothing but a stolen rifle and a price on their head. The resistance gave them shelter, and XCOM gave them a purpose. Now they use their technical knowledge to dismantle the alien occupation, one machine at a time.

Before the invasion, they were a competitive marksman who dreamed of joining the military. When ADVENT seized control, their skills became a means of survival. They joined a resistance cell, serving as a sniper and patiently eliminating patrol leaders from rooftops and ruined buildings. During one mission, their entire team was ambushed, leaving them the sole survivor. Haunted by the loss, they became distant and methodical. XCOM recruited them for their exceptional accuracy. Now every shot is deliberate, every target chosen carefully. They refuse to let another squad die because they missed.

Once a street racer and petty smuggler, they knew every back alley and forgotten road in their city. When ADVENT tightened its grip, they used those skills to transport resistance fighters and supplies past checkpoints. After a convoy ambush exposed their operation, they barely escaped capture. With nowhere left to hide, they joined XCOM, trading stolen vehicles for military hardware. They may bend the rules, but when bullets start flying, their loyalty is unquestionable.

Raised in an isolated settlement, they grew up hunting to keep their community fed. When ADVENT forces discovered the settlement, they returned home to find it burned and its inhabitants missing. Alone and driven by grief, they tracked the patrol responsible and struck back with improvised traps and patient ambushes. The resistance eventually found them living off the land. XCOM offered training, weapons, and a chance to fight back on a larger scale. They accepted without hesitation.

Once a respected police officer, they refused to accept ADVENT's new order when they witnessed civilians being dragged away for questioning. Branded a traitor, they escaped arrest and joined the resistance, using their knowledge of urban combat and interrogation tactics to expose collaborators. Years of betrayal have left them distrustful of authority, but they still believe in protecting the innocent. XCOM may be humanity's last hope, and they intend to make every shot count.

They were once a promising scientist working on alien technology under ADVENT supervision. When they discovered evidence that the so-called Elders were conducting horrific experiments on humans, they attempted to leak the findings. Their colleagues vanished overnight, and they narrowly escaped the same fate. A resistance contact smuggled them to safety, where their technical expertise proved invaluable. Now fighting alongside XCOM, they use their knowledge of the enemy to turn alien weapons against their creators.

They grew up idolizing the soldiers who once protected their homeland, never imagining they would one day fight an occupying force themselves. When ADVENT raided their neighborhood, they escaped by hiding among the dead. Rescued by resistance fighters, they trained relentlessly, determined never to feel helpless again. Their discipline and courage earned them a place in XCOM. Though inexperienced compared to veteran soldiers, they possess an unshakable resolve: humanity will not surrender while they still draw breath.

Once a professional thief, they survived the occupation by stealing from ADVENT supply depots and selling information to the resistance. Their luck ran out when a heist uncovered a secret detention facility. Unable to ignore the prisoners inside, they sabotaged the security systems and helped them escape. The resistance offered them a choice: keep running or fight back. They chose XCOM, bringing sharp instincts, steady hands, and a talent for getting into places they shouldn't.

They were a former professional athlete whose career ended when ADVENT's occupation destroyed the facilities where they trained. Refusing to become another obedient citizen, they joined an underground resistance network, using their speed and endurance to carry messages through hostile territory. After surviving a mission that left their entire team captured, they swore never to be powerless again. XCOM gave them the weapons and training they lacked. Now they channel their competitive spirit into a single goal: defeating the invaders.

They once worked as a firefighter, running toward danger while others fled. When ADVENT bombed a resistance hideout, they joined the rescue effort, pulling survivors from the rubble under enemy fire. Witnessing the occupation's cruelty firsthand, they abandoned their old life and joined the resistance. Their calm under pressure and instinct to protect others caught XCOM's attention. Though they still carry the guilt of those they couldn't save, they fight on, determined to give humanity a chance to rebuild.

They were a radio operator who spent the occupation intercepting ADVENT communications for the resistance. One night, they detected a transmission revealing an imminent raid on their safehouse. Their warning saved dozens of lives, but exposed their identity to enemy intelligence. Forced into hiding, they eventually joined XCOM, bringing invaluable expertise in signals and electronic warfare. They rarely speak of their past, preferring to listen, analyze, and strike when the enemy least expects it.

They were a quiet schoolteacher who secretly taught students the truth about humanity's past, forbidden under ADVENT rule. When authorities discovered the lessons, they arrested several families and branded the teacher a dangerous dissident. Forced to flee, they joined the resistance, using their organizational skills to coordinate evacuations and protect civilians. XCOM later recruited them for their courage and level-headed judgment. They fight not out of hatred, but to ensure the next generation grows up free to think, question, and choose.

They were once a mountain rescue specialist, skilled at navigating hostile terrain and finding people others had given up on. When ADVENT occupied their region, they used forgotten trails to smuggle refugees past patrols. After a mission ended in an ambush, they lost contact with their group and survived alone for weeks. XCOM eventually discovered their hideout and offered them a place in the resistance. They accepted, determined to make sure no one else gets left behind in enemy territory.

Once a military intelligence analyst, they spent years studying enemy movements and predicting threats from behind a desk. When ADVENT uncovered their resistance contacts, they were forced to flee and leave their old life behind. Determined to put theory into practice, they underwent combat training and joined XCOM. Their ability to anticipate enemy tactics makes them a valuable asset, though they struggle with the uncertainty of battle. For the first time, humanity's survival depends on more than their calculations.

They were a cargo pilot who smuggled medicine and refugees through ADVENT-controlled airspace. After refusing to transport prisoners to an unknown facility, they were branded a criminal and their aircraft was shot down. They survived the crash and were rescued by resistance fighters. With their flying days behind them, they took up arms instead. XCOM offered a chance to strike back at the regime that destroyed their life. They intend to make every mission count, wherever the fight takes them.

They were a former underground boxer who learned early that survival often depended on taking the first hit and staying standing. When ADVENT raided their neighborhood, they fought back to protect civilians, drawing the attention of resistance recruiters. Years of discipline and hard-earned endurance made them a formidable close-quarters fighter. Joining XCOM gave them a chance to turn raw toughness into a real weapon. They know they cannot save everyone, but they refuse to stop fighting while anyone still needs protecting.

They were an archaeologist studying an ancient civilization when the invasion began. Their research was seized by ADVENT, who claimed it contained evidence of humanity's supposed destiny under the Elders. Refusing to let history be rewritten, they escaped with stolen records and joined the resistance. Their knowledge of alien artifacts soon proved useful to XCOM. Fascinated by the enemy but never fooled by its promises, they fight to uncover the truth behind the invasion and reclaim humanity's future.

They grew up in a remote farming community that survived by avoiding ADVENT's attention. When soldiers arrived to seize the settlement's food supplies, the locals resisted and were slaughtered as an example to others. Hidden in a grain silo, they survived by chance alone. With nowhere to return, they joined the resistance, turning years of hunting and farm work into practical combat skills. Now fighting with XCOM, they carry the memory of their lost home into every battle, determined that no community should suffer the same fate.

Once a prison guard under ADVENT rule, they followed orders until witnessing prisoners being taken away for experiments. Unable to ignore what they had seen, they secretly helped several detainees escape, sacrificing their position and becoming a fugitive. The resistance gave them shelter, but trust had to be earned. After proving their loyalty in several dangerous operations, they were recruited by XCOM. They now fight to atone for their past, determined never again to stand on the wrong side of a cell door.

They survived the invasion by working as a black-market trader, exchanging stolen ADVENT supplies for food, medicine, and information. When a deal went wrong, they were captured and interrogated, but refused to reveal their resistance contacts. After escaping during a transport ambush, they finally abandoned their life of profiteering and joined XCOM. Resourceful, persuasive, and accustomed to danger, they know that survival sometimes requires dirty hands—but this time, they're fighting for something greater than themselves.

They were a paramedic when an ADVENT attack overwhelmed the city hospital where they worked. With supplies running low and enemy patrols blocking evacuation routes, they organized survivors and led them through the ruins to safety. The experience taught them that courage meant acting even when terrified. After joining the resistance, they learned to fight as well as heal. XCOM recruited them for their composure under fire. They still carry medical supplies into battle, determined to bring as many comrades home as possible.

They were a graffiti artist who turned city walls into silent acts of rebellion, painting symbols that mocked ADVENT propaganda and inspired hope among the occupied. When their work exposed a hidden resistance network, they were forced to flee and take up arms. Their knowledge of urban terrain proved invaluable during guerrilla operations. Recruited by XCOM, they now fight in the open, carrying the same defiant spirit that once painted walls. To them, every liberated city is another message the Elders cannot erase.

They were a deep-sea salvage diver when ADVENT began searching the oceans for remnants of alien technology. Hired to recover a mysterious wreck, they discovered human prisoners sealed inside a submerged facility. They freed as many as they could before the structure collapsed, escaping with evidence of ADVENT's crimes. The resistance helped them disappear, and XCOM later recruited them for their nerve and resourcefulness. Accustomed to darkness and pressure, they now face a different kind of abyss: the war for humanity's survival.

They once worked as a journalist, documenting the quiet disappearances and suspicious deaths hidden beneath ADVENT's promises of peace. When their investigation uncovered evidence of alien experiments, government censors branded them a terrorist and sent soldiers to silence them. Forced underground, they passed their findings to the resistance and learned to survive on the run. XCOM recruited them for their determination and sharp instincts. Now they expose the truth with a rifle, fighting to ensure humanity never forgets what was done to it.

They were a former competitive fencer whose precision and reflexes caught the attention of a resistance recruiter. When ADVENT raided their training hall for suspected dissidents, they escaped by disarming a soldier and stealing their weapon. Forced to abandon their old life, they adapted quickly to firearms and battlefield tactics. XCOM offered the training they needed to turn instinct into discipline. They now approach every firefight like a duel: study the opponent, find the opening, and strike without hesitation.

They were a train engineer who secretly used supply routes to smuggle resistance fighters through ADVENT checkpoints. When an informant exposed the operation, they derailed a military transport to cover the passengers' escape. The sabotage cost them their livelihood and made them a wanted fugitive. The resistance helped them disappear before XCOM recruited them for their technical skills and courage. Now they sabotage alien logistics with the same ingenuity, determined to keep the occupation from crushing another generation.

They were a former stage magician whose career depended on misdirection, quick hands, and reading an audience. Under ADVENT, those tricks became tools for survival, helping them smuggle supplies and forge security credentials. When a resistance mission went wrong, they improvised an escape that saved an entire cell. XCOM recruited them for their creativity and nerves under pressure. On the battlefield, they use deception and unconventional tactics to keep the enemy guessing, proving that sometimes the deadliest weapon is a well-timed illusion.

They were a meteorologist studying increasingly strange weather patterns when ADVENT seized their research station. Their data revealed that alien infrastructure was altering Earth's atmosphere, but the discovery was dismissed as conspiracy. After escaping captivity with stolen records, they joined the resistance. XCOM valued their analytical mind and ability to predict environmental hazards. Though not a natural soldier, they learned quickly, driven by the belief that saving humanity means protecting not just its people, but the planet they call home.

They were a former stunt performer, accustomed to dangerous falls, explosions, and split-second decisions. When ADVENT raided a film set suspected of hiding resistance members, they used their training to lead the crew through a collapsing building. The escape caught the attention of local rebels, who recruited them for high-risk missions. XCOM later offered proper combat training. Fear never disappeared, but they learned to work through it, treating every battlefield like the most dangerous performance of their life—except this time, the stakes are real.

They were a wildlife ranger protecting a remote nature reserve when ADVENT began clearing forests for an alien research facility. Refusing to abandon the animals and nearby villagers, they sabotaged construction equipment and guided civilians through hidden trails. Hunted by security forces, they eventually joined the resistance. Their tracking skills and patience made them a natural scout for XCOM. They now hunt the invaders across ruined cities and wild terrain, determined to defend a world that cannot fight back for itself.

They were a locksmith who secretly helped resistance members escape detention by forging keys and bypassing security systems. When ADVENT discovered their activities, they were forced to flee after narrowly escaping arrest. The resistance offered protection in exchange for their expertise, and XCOM soon recognized their talent for infiltration. Patient, observant, and skilled at finding weaknesses, they approach every mission like a locked door waiting to be opened. They intend to make sure the Elders' empire comes crashing down, one breach at a time.

They were a former disaster relief volunteer who traveled wherever conflict left people desperate for help. When ADVENT began restricting aid to compliant settlements, they defied orders and delivered supplies to resistance sympathizers. After their team was arrested, they escaped and joined the underground. Years of working in ruined cities taught them to stay calm amid chaos and improvise with limited resources. XCOM gave them the means to fight the source of humanity's suffering rather than merely treating its wounds.

Once a professional gambler, they survived the occupation by reading people, spotting patterns, and knowing when to take a risk. Their luck changed when they overheard ADVENT officers discussing a planned raid on a resistance hideout. Rather than walk away, they warned the rebels and helped organize an ambush. Impressed by their nerve and instincts, the resistance offered them a place in the fight. XCOM soon followed. They still gamble with the odds, but now the stakes are humanity's future.

They were a deep-cover informant who spent years feeding false intelligence to ADVENT while protecting a network of resistance sympathizers. When their handler grew suspicious, they were forced to flee before their identity was exposed. With nowhere left to hide, they approached XCOM and offered everything they knew. Years of deception left them guarded and difficult to trust, but their intelligence has saved countless lives. Now they fight openly for the first time, determined to bring down the system they once infiltrated.

They were a former search-and-rescue volunteer who specialized in locating survivors after disasters. When ADVENT destroyed a resistance safehouse, they joined the recovery effort and discovered that several missing people had been taken to a secret detention center. Unable to accept the authorities' lies, they helped plan a rescue operation. Their courage earned them a place in XCOM. Now they search battlefields for the living and fight to ensure that no one disappears without a trace again.

They were a former emergency dispatcher who learned to stay calm while others panicked. During an ADVENT assault on their city, they coordinated civilian evacuations until enemy forces traced the signals to their station. Forced to flee, they joined the resistance and used their knowledge of communications to guide fighters through hostile territory. XCOM recruited them for their quick thinking and composure under pressure. Now, instead of directing others through the chaos, they face it firsthand, determined to answer every call for help they can reach.

Once a stage technician, they specialized in lighting, rigging, and pyrotechnics. When ADVENT shut down the theaters, they turned abandoned venues into resistance hideouts, using traps and improvised explosives to deter patrols. After one hideout was discovered, they stayed behind to trigger a controlled collapse, buying their comrades time to escape. XCOM recruited them for their ingenuity and nerve. They now use the battlefield as a stage, where every distraction is deliberate and every explosion has a purpose.

They were a former military chaplain who stayed behind during the invasion to help civilians trapped in a besieged town. When ADVENT forces stormed their shelter, they took up a fallen soldier's weapon to defend the survivors. Though they escaped, the violence haunted them. The resistance later offered them a place among its fighters. They joined XCOM not out of hatred, but conviction that protecting life sometimes requires confronting those who threaten it. Before every mission, they take a moment to remember the fallen.

They were a professional locksmith who specialized in high-security systems before ADVENT took control. When a resistance contact asked for help breaking into a detention facility, they agreed, expecting a simple job. Instead, they found prisoners scheduled for transport to an unknown destination. They helped free them and became a fugitive overnight. XCOM recruited them for their technical skills and steady nerves. Now they specialize in breaching fortified positions, proving that even the strongest locks have weaknesses—and so does the alien empire.

They were a former mountain climber who made a living guiding expeditions through dangerous terrain. When ADVENT established a remote listening post in the mountains, they discovered prisoners being transported along hidden trails. Using their knowledge of the cliffs and weather, they helped a resistance team ambush the convoy and free the captives. Their courage earned them a place in XCOM. Comfortable with heights, isolation, and impossible odds, they now take the paths others consider too dangerous to attempt.

They were a former investigative accountant who uncovered suspicious payments funding ADVENT's secret research programs. Before they could expose the evidence, their employer reported them to the authorities. Forced to flee, they smuggled financial records to the resistance, revealing several hidden facilities. XCOM recruited them for their sharp mind and attention to detail. Though no soldier by training, they quickly learned to handle a weapon. They now hunt the people behind the numbers, determined to make the architects of the occupation answer for their crimes.

They were a former professional drummer whose touring career ended when ADVENT imposed strict controls on public gatherings. They began organizing secret performances that doubled as resistance meetings, using music to pass coded messages between cells. When security forces raided a show, they escaped through the backstage tunnels but lost several friends to arrest. The resistance helped them disappear, and XCOM offered a chance to fight openly. They still keep rhythm under fire, believing that as long as humanity resists, its heartbeat cannot be silenced.

They were a former wildlife photographer who documented the destruction caused by ADVENT's expansion. While photographing a restricted zone, they captured evidence of civilians being used in alien experiments. Their images made them a target, forcing them to flee into the wilderness. The resistance sheltered them, and their patience, sharp eyes, and ability to remain unseen proved invaluable. XCOM recruited them as a scout. They still carry a camera alongside their rifle, determined to record the truth when humanity finally wins its freedom.

They were a former courier who delivered packages across occupied territory, asking no questions. One delivery changed everything: inside the sealed container were weapons intended for an ADVENT-backed militia. Rather than complete the job, they stole the cargo and delivered it to the resistance. Hunted by their former employers, they learned to fight while constantly on the move. XCOM eventually recruited them for their speed, street knowledge, and nerve. They still prefer action over explanations, but their loyalties are no longer for sale.

They were a former competitive chess player who learned to think several moves ahead. Under ADVENT's occupation, they used that talent to plan supply thefts and predict patrol routes for a small resistance cell. When an ambush went wrong, they improvised a daring escape that saved most of the team. XCOM recruited them for their tactical instincts and cool head under pressure. They know war is more than a game, but every enemy has weaknesses—and they intend to find them before the next move costs another life.

They were a former deep-cover police investigator who spent years infiltrating criminal networks under ADVENT's watchful eye. When they discovered that local authorities were secretly trafficking dissidents to alien facilities, their superiors ordered them to forget what they had seen. Instead, they leaked the evidence and disappeared. The resistance offered protection, and XCOM gave them a new mission. Skilled at reading people and spotting lies, they trust actions over promises and intend to expose every secret the Elders are hiding.

They were a former demolition worker who helped clear buildings for ADVENT's redevelopment projects. After discovering that evacuated neighborhoods were being converted into secret detention sites, they began sabotaging construction equipment and freeing prisoners. When their activities were exposed, they escaped with the resistance. Their knowledge of explosives and structural weaknesses made them an ideal recruit for XCOM. Practical and unshakable, they believe every fortress can fall if you know where to place the charge.

They were a former radio astronomer who detected strange signals long before the invasion. Their warnings were dismissed, and their research was confiscated when ADVENT took control. Years later, they discovered that the signals matched transmissions from alien installations. After escaping an attempt to silence them, they joined the resistance. XCOM recruited them for their technical expertise and relentless curiosity. Now they hunt the source of the transmissions, determined to understand the enemy before humanity loses its last chance.

They grew up in a traveling circus, learning acrobatics, balance, and how to stay calm when everything went wrong. After ADVENT shut down the troupe for refusing to perform propaganda shows, they joined a resistance cell and used their agility to scout rooftops and cross dangerous terrain. During a raid, they led several civilians to safety through collapsing buildings. XCOM recognized their reflexes and fearlessness. Though the battlefield is no stage, they still thrive where others hesitate, turning impossible odds into opportunities.

They were a former chef who secretly fed resistance fighters from the kitchen of an ADVENT-controlled facility. When they discovered that missing workers were being sent to alien experiments, they poisoned a shipment of supplies to delay the operation and helped several prisoners escape. Forced to abandon their old life, they joined the resistance. XCOM recruited them for their courage and resourcefulness. They may not look like a soldier, but they know that survival depends on preparation, timing, and making every resource count.

They were a former competitive archer who lived quietly until ADVENT began forcibly recruiting civilians for its security forces. Refusing to serve the occupation, they fled into the forests and joined a resistance cell, using patience and precision to eliminate patrols from a distance. After a mission exposed their position, XCOM rescued the surviving fighters and offered them a place in its ranks. They adapted to modern weapons quickly, but still approach every shot with the same discipline: breathe, focus, and never waste an opportunity.

They were a former urban explorer who mapped abandoned tunnels beneath major cities. When ADVENT began using the underground network to move prisoners unnoticed, they offered their knowledge to the resistance. During a rescue mission, they guided a squad through forgotten passages and led dozens of captives to freedom. XCOM recruited them for their navigation skills and ability to remain calm in confined spaces. They know the world above may belong to the aliens, but beneath their feet lies a maze the Elders will never fully control.

They were a former disaster-response engineer who specialized in keeping critical infrastructure running during crises. When ADVENT deliberately shut down power and water to rebellious districts, they secretly restored essential services and helped civilians escape. After their network was exposed, they fled and joined the resistance. XCOM recruited them for their practical skills and calm decision-making. They understand that wars are won not only by destroying the enemy, but by keeping people alive long enough to see victory.

They were a former prison escape artist whose unusual skills attracted attention from the resistance. When ADVENT transferred political prisoners to a fortified detention center, they volunteered to infiltrate it and guide captives out. The operation nearly failed, but their quick thinking saved the team. XCOM later recruited them for their ingenuity and ability to improvise under pressure. They approach every mission as a puzzle with a solution, convinced that no cage, security system, or alien empire is truly unbreakable.

They were a former long-haul trucker who learned to navigate the occupied world through back roads and forgotten checkpoints. For years, they smuggled medicine and refugees past ADVENT patrols, until a convoy was ambushed and their closest friend was killed. Rather than run, they joined the resistance and began striking back. XCOM recruited them for their endurance, practical instincts, and knowledge of enemy logistics. They still prefer the open road, but now their destination is a world free from alien rule.

They were a former forensic technician who noticed disturbing inconsistencies in official reports about civilians killed during ADVENT operations. Their investigation uncovered evidence of alien experiments disguised as routine medical procedures. Before they could expose the truth, security forces raided their laboratory. They escaped with stolen files and sought refuge with the resistance. XCOM recruited them for their analytical mind and attention to detail. They now examine every battlefield carefully, determined to uncover the truth behind the occupation and bring its architects to justice.

They were a former competitive fencer whose quick reflexes and discipline made them a natural duelist. When ADVENT forces raided their training academy, they fought long enough for their fellow students to escape. Forced into hiding, they joined the resistance and adapted their precise movements to modern combat. XCOM recruited them for their composure under pressure and fearless approach to close encounters. They know every fight carries risks, but they refuse to let the enemy dictate the terms of engagement.

They were a former botanist studying plants that survived in heavily polluted environments. When ADVENT began poisoning farmland to force settlements into compliance, they joined a resistance effort to protect local food supplies. Their improvised solutions kept hundreds alive, but eventually drew enemy attention. Forced to abandon their laboratory, they took up arms alongside the rebels they had helped. XCOM recruited them for their resourcefulness and patience. They fight to restore a world where humanity can grow roots again without fear.

They were a former locksmith who specialized in antique mechanisms and forgotten security systems. When the resistance needed access to an ADVENT archive, they volunteered to bypass its defenses. Inside, they discovered records of civilians marked for experimentation and barely escaped the facility alive. The resistance welcomed them, and XCOM soon recruited their unique skills. Patient and meticulous, they approach every fortified position as a challenge to solve. They intend to unlock the secrets of the alien occupation—and ensure its doors close forever.

They were a former competitive swimmer who worked as a salvage diver after the invasion. While exploring a flooded military base, they discovered an abandoned resistance cache containing weapons and intelligence. ADVENT patrols cornered them before they could escape, forcing them to fight their way out through submerged tunnels. Impressed by their endurance and composure, the resistance offered them a place in its ranks. XCOM later recruited them for dangerous operations where stamina and calm under pressure can mean the difference between life and death.

They were a former courtroom interpreter who witnessed ADVENT officials twisting testimony to justify the disappearance of political dissidents. When they secretly recorded evidence of the fraud, security forces raided their home. They escaped with the recordings and passed them to the resistance, exposing a network of collaborators. XCOM recruited them for their sharp memory and ability to recognize deception. They now fight against a regime built on lies, determined to ensure that humanity's final judgment is delivered on the battlefield.

They were a former parkour instructor who taught young people to navigate rooftops and abandoned buildings. When ADVENT sealed their district during a resistance sweep, they guided a group of students across the city without being detected. Their escape route saved dozens, but left them marked as an enemy of the regime. The resistance offered shelter, and XCOM later recruited them for their agility and spatial awareness. They now move through battlefields with the same confidence they once taught on rooftops, always searching for the next opening.

They were a former veterinarian who secretly treated injured resistance fighters alongside abandoned animals in a makeshift clinic. When ADVENT discovered the operation, they destroyed the clinic and arrested several volunteers. Escaping with a handful of patients, they joined the resistance and learned to defend those under their care. XCOM recruited them for their steady hands and compassion under pressure. Though the battlefield is far removed from their old practice, they still believe every life saved is another small victory against the occupation.

They once worked as a casino security specialist, trained to spot suspicious behavior and react before trouble started. When ADVENT officers began using the casino to identify potential dissidents, they secretly warned targeted civilians and helped them escape. Their actions exposed a network of informants, forcing them to disappear. The resistance recruited them for their sharp instincts and composure under pressure. Now serving with XCOM, they watch every movement carefully, knowing that the smallest detail can reveal an enemy's next move.

They were a former lighthouse keeper living on a remote coast, guiding ships through dangerous waters. When ADVENT began using the coastline for covert transports, they secretly signaled resistance vessels and helped refugees escape by sea. After an enemy patrol discovered the operation, they destroyed the lighthouse equipment and fled inland. XCOM recruited them for their patience, vigilance, and ability to remain alert through long nights. They now keep watch over a different horizon, waiting for the moment humanity can finally reclaim its world.

They were a former locksmith who made a living restoring antique safes and security systems. When a resistance contact asked them to open a confiscated ADVENT vault, they discovered evidence of secret experiments on captured civilians. Before they could escape, security forces arrived, forcing them to fight their way out. The resistance offered protection, and XCOM recognized their steady hands and problem-solving skills. They now specialize in breaching enemy defenses, determined to expose every secret the Elders have buried.

They were a former competitive snowboarder who made a living performing dangerous stunts in remote mountains. When ADVENT established a hidden facility nearby, they discovered supply convoys moving through forgotten passes. They began feeding their routes to the resistance, using their knowledge of the terrain to guide ambushes. After an operation went wrong, XCOM offered them a place among its ranks. Fearless on difficult ground, they now bring their balance, reflexes, and appetite for risk to the fight against the Elders.

They were a former museum conservator who secretly hid artifacts confiscated by ADVENT from occupied communities. While cataloguing an alien relic, they discovered records linking it to a nearby detention facility. They passed the evidence to the resistance, then helped organize a raid to free the prisoners. Their knowledge of alien technology caught XCOM's attention. Though more accustomed to delicate tools than firearms, they have learned to fight with determination, believing humanity's history deserves a future beyond the Elders' control.

They were a former courier for a rural postal service, traveling forgotten roads between isolated settlements. When ADVENT began intercepting civilian communications, they started carrying secret messages for the resistance instead. One delivery exposed a planned raid, allowing an entire village to evacuate before the soldiers arrived. Their network eventually collapsed, forcing them to flee and join XCOM. They still believe that even the smallest message can change the course of a war, and they intend to deliver humanity's answer to the Elders personally.

Once a geological surveyor mapping remote mineral deposits, they discovered ADVENT had been concealing evidence of underground facilities beneath abandoned mines. When their research team vanished after reporting the findings, they escaped with stolen data and spent months sabotaging supply routes in the wilderness. XCOM eventually tracked their transmissions and offered them a chance to turn their knowledge of the underground into a weapon against the occupation.

A former emergency room nurse, they spent the occupation treating civilians in an overcrowded underground clinic. When ADVENT began rounding up patients suspected of aiding the resistance, they forged medical records and smuggled the vulnerable to safety. After the clinic was raided, they escaped with a bag of stolen supplies and joined a resistance cell. Their steady hands and ability to function under pressure soon earned them a place among XCOM’s frontline soldiers.

Before the invasion, they worked as an industrial crane operator at a busy shipping port. When ADVENT seized the docks, they secretly used heavy machinery to disrupt shipments of alien technology and create escape routes for trapped civilians. After their sabotage exposed them, they fled with a group of dockworkers and joined the resistance. Their experience handling massive equipment and staying calm under pressure made them a valuable addition to XCOM.

Once a professional storm chaser, they spent years tracking violent weather across remote regions. After the invasion, ADVENT began exploiting abandoned weather stations to monitor resistance movements. Using their knowledge of atmospheric systems, they sabotaged the network and helped insurgents move undetected during severe storms. When a mission went wrong and their team was scattered, they fought their way to an XCOM rendezvous, bringing valuable intelligence and nerves hardened by years of facing nature’s fury.

Before the invasion, they were a competitive drone racing pilot known for navigating impossibly tight courses at incredible speed. When ADVENT repurposed civilian drones for surveillance, they began modifying racing models to scout patrols and deliver supplies to resistance hideouts. After an intercepted flight exposed their operation, they escaped a citywide manhunt and joined XCOM. Their reflexes, spatial awareness, and instinct for finding gaps in enemy defenses proved invaluable in the field.

XCOM now relies on their ability to follow money, expose hidden networks, and identify which enemy officers can be bribed or blackmailed.

A former competitive cheese maker, this soldier supplied specialty foods to an ADVENT-controlled luxury market. They discovered the refrigeration facility was secretly storing alien specimens alongside the merchandise. When a containment failure killed the staff, ADVENT planned to blame local farmers and sterilize the entire district. They sabotaged the facility’s cooling systems to destroy the evidence and escaped through its delivery tunnels. The resistance recruited them for their technical ingenuity and intimate knowledge of industrial refrigeration systems.

A former sign language instructor, this soldier taught deaf civilians to communicate after ADVENT outlawed unregistered communication devices. Their classes became a covert resistance network, passing warnings through gestures hidden in crowded streets. When an informant exposed the group, they stayed behind to mislead the patrols, allowing their students to escape. Captured and interrogated, they refused to reveal the network's safehouses before making a daring escape. XCOM recruited them for their composure under pressure and ability to coordinate silently when radio contact is impossible.

A former competitive glass harmonica performer, this soldier was recruited to entertain ADVENT officials at private functions. They discovered that certain tones triggered unusual responses in nearby Sectoid test subjects, revealing a weakness in their neural conditioning. After secretly recording the effect, they sabotaged a laboratory demonstration and escaped with the research data. ADVENT branded them a dangerous agitator. The resistance smuggled them to safety, and XCOM now hopes their discovery can help disrupt alien mind-control techniques.

A former urban beekeeper, this soldier maintained rooftop hives that helped pollinate abandoned city gardens. When ADVENT introduced a pesticide to eliminate supposedly contaminated insects, they discovered it was designed to poison crops and increase dependence on government food supplies. They hid surviving colonies in underground gardens and sabotaged the chemical distribution center. Forced to flee after a security raid, they joined the resistance, bringing expertise in improvised toxins, environmental sabotage, and surviving off the land.

A former competitive sand sculptor, this soldier worked on elaborate monuments for ADVENT propaganda festivals. While constructing a display near a restricted zone, they noticed supply trucks entering a building that officially stood abandoned. They investigated after dark and discovered a covert facility manufacturing false identities for alien infiltrators. Before escaping, they stole a set of personnel files and destroyed the printing equipment. The resistance used the files to expose several compromised officials, and XCOM recruited them for their stealth, patience, and talent for spotting tiny inconsistencies.

A former cave acoustics researcher, this soldier mapped underground chambers for a geothermal energy project. During a survey, they detected rhythmic signals echoing from a sealed cavern and discovered an abandoned alien relay station beneath the rock. ADVENT troops arrived to reactivate it, forcing them to collapse the entrance and flee with their recordings. The resistance recognized the signals as part of a hidden communications network. Now serving with XCOM, they use their knowledge of sound, echoes, and subterranean terrain to locate concealed facilities and ambush enemy patrols.

A former meteorite curator, this soldier managed a small museum that ADVENT converted into a center for alien artifact research. While cataloguing a newly recovered specimen, they discovered it emitted pulses that disrupted nearby surveillance systems. They hid fragments in ordinary display cases and smuggled them out during a staged evacuation. When ADVENT uncovered the theft, they destroyed the remaining collection and vanished into the countryside. XCOM recruited them to study the fragments and exploit their strange effects against alien technology.

A former competitive locksmith specializing in antique mechanisms, this soldier was hired to open a sealed vault beneath an abandoned courthouse. Inside, they found evidence that ADVENT had been secretly transferring prisoners under falsified death certificates. Before security forces arrived, they memorized the records and rigged the vault to lock behind them. They escaped through maintenance tunnels and delivered the information to a resistance cell. XCOM recruited them for their steady hands, mechanical intuition, and ability to bypass security without leaving a trace.

A former deep-sea archaeologist, this soldier discovered an alien structure buried beneath the ruins of a flooded coastal city. Its walls contained records of human settlements dating back centuries before ADVENT’s arrival. When alien forces moved to retrieve the site, they flooded the excavation to conceal it. The soldier escaped with a fragment of the structure’s data core, surviving days in submerged tunnels before reaching the resistance. XCOM now relies on their expertise to investigate ancient alien technology and uncover secrets the invaders hoped would remain buried.

A former professional puppeteer, this soldier performed at shelters for children displaced by ADVENT’s resettlement programs. They began hiding coded evacuation instructions inside their shows, using puppet movements to signal safe routes and patrol schedules. When ADVENT raided a performance, they improvised a diversion that let dozens of families escape through the backstage tunnels. Their network was exposed, forcing them into hiding. The resistance recruited them for their quick thinking, misdirection skills, and knack for coordinating people without electronic communication.

A former forensic linguist, this soldier analyzed intercepted broadcasts for signs of fabricated resistance activity. They discovered ADVENT was using stolen voices to create false surrender orders, luring rebel groups into ambushes. After warning several cells, they infiltrated a transmission hub and destroyed its voice archive before escaping under fire. With their research dismissed as enemy propaganda, they joined XCOM, determined to expose deception and ensure no soldier dies trusting a familiar voice at the wrong moment.

A former volcanologist, this soldier monitored seismic activity near an ADVENT geothermal plant. Their instruments revealed deliberate underground detonations designed to trigger a collapse beneath a crowded settlement. Unable to convince the authorities, they sabotaged the plant’s control systems and guided residents through old lava tubes moments before the disaster. ADVENT blamed them for the destruction and issued an arrest order. The resistance took them in, and XCOM gained an expert at reading unstable terrain, predicting structural failures, and turning the battlefield itself against the enemy.

A former theatrical costume maker, this soldier secretly altered ADVENT uniforms to help resistance couriers pass through checkpoints unnoticed. Their work unraveled when a disguised courier infiltrated a supply depot and uncovered plans for a mass arrest. When security traced the forged uniforms to their workshop, they set the building ablaze and escaped through a drainage canal. The resistance offered them a new home, and XCOM now benefits from their talent for disguise, improvisation, and recognizing the small details that give an infiltrator away.

A former competitive glider pilot, this soldier delivered medical supplies between isolated settlements after ADVENT restricted civilian air travel. During one flight, they spotted an off-the-books convoy transporting captives toward a remote processing facility. They diverted their route, dropped supplies to a nearby resistance cell, and guided the rebels to intercept the convoy. ADVENT grounded every civilian aircraft in the region, but the pilot escaped with a stolen glider. XCOM recruited them for their aerial instincts, nerve under fire, and ability to navigate without electronic guidance.

A former stained-glass artist, this soldier repaired windows in an abandoned cathedral converted into an ADVENT archive. Hidden behind a shattered panel, they discovered a cache of handwritten accounts from civilians who had witnessed early alien experiments. They copied the testimonies and used colored glass fragments to mark a secret escape route for imprisoned archivists. When ADVENT discovered the theft, they fled through the cathedral’s crypts. The resistance recruited them for their patience, steady hands, and talent for spotting patterns others overlook.

A former railway dining-car chef, this soldier used supply runs to smuggle medicine and forged travel permits between occupied cities. One night, they discovered a sealed compartment containing sedated civilians destined for an ADVENT experimentation site. They uncoupled the car during a scheduled stop and guided the captives into the surrounding countryside. Branded a saboteur, they survived by moving between resistance safehouses. XCOM recruited them for their resourcefulness, knowledge of transport networks, and ability to stay calm when a carefully timed plan falls apart.

A former taxidermist, this soldier preserved rare specimens for an ADVENT-funded natural history institute. While preparing an alien creature brought in under armed guard, they found a tracking implant embedded beneath its skin. Its serial markings matched devices recovered from missing civilians. They stole the implant and released the remaining specimens during a staged power failure, creating enough chaos to escape. The resistance recruited them for their steady hands, knowledge of alien anatomy, and ability to identify technology concealed inside living tissue.

A former professional kite designer, this soldier built oversized signal kites to communicate between resistance camps beyond ADVENT’s surveillance grid. During a storm, they spotted an alien dropship struggling with damaged guidance systems and realized the wind currents could disrupt its landing approach. They relayed the pattern to nearby rebels, who ambushed the grounded craft and rescued its prisoners. ADVENT destroyed their workshop, but the designer escaped with their plans. XCOM recruited them for their ingenuity, weather sense, and talent for exploiting environmental weaknesses.

A former elevator inspector, this soldier discovered that an ADVENT residential tower’s emergency lifts were being rerouted to an unlisted underground facility. They entered during a maintenance shift and found prisoners held beneath the building, their disappearances concealed by falsified evacuation records. They disabled the lift controls, triggering a building-wide lockdown that gave the captives time to escape through service shafts. Hunted by security forces, they joined the resistance, bringing XCOM expertise in vertical access, mechanical sabotage, and navigating sealed structures.

A former competitive cheese-racing organizer, this soldier managed rural festivals that ADVENT used to monitor civilian gatherings. They noticed security teams quietly replacing food shipments with sealed containers bound for a nearby research complex. After sneaking inside, they found evidence of experiments on livestock exposed to alien compounds. They leaked the records and sabotaged the transport depot before escaping on a delivery tractor. The resistance recruited them for their rural contacts, practical ingenuity, and knack for moving unnoticed through supposedly harmless communities.

Before the invasion, a former court stenographer. This soldier secretly recorded an ADVENT tribunal where officials discussed using fabricated charges to disappear political dissidents. Before the recordings could be confiscated, they memorized the testimony and hid coded transcripts inside routine legal filings. When an imprisoned witness was scheduled for execution, they leaked the evidence to the resistance, triggering a daring prison extraction. Forced underground, they joined XCOM, bringing exceptional recall, attention to detail, and a determination to make the occupation answer for its crimes.

The first time the sky went dark, this soldier was halfway through repairing a planetarium projector. The blackout revealed something impossible: dozens of lights moving in formation beyond the clouds, invisible to ADVENT tracking systems. They rebuilt the projector into an improvised observation device and tracked the lights to a concealed alien relay. Before ADVENT seized the equipment, they transmitted its coordinates to the resistance. They never studied astronomy again. Now they watch the skies for threats humanity doesn't yet know exist.

Nobody believed the cemetery groundskeeper when the graves began appearing empty. ADVENT blamed vandals, but the disturbed soil showed the bodies had been removed from below. One night, the groundskeeper followed a maintenance crew into an unmarked tunnel and found a hidden transport route carrying the dead to an alien research site. They escaped with a stolen access card, leaving the tunnel entrance buried beneath a fresh grave. The resistance used the card to raid the facility. The groundskeeper never returned to tending graves—there were too many living people left to save.

The theater was already burning when the stage magician realized the fire wasn't part of the show. ADVENT troops had arrived to arrest an actor who'd been passing resistance messages through scripted dialogue. With the exits blocked, the magician improvised an escape using trapdoors, smoke charges, and a collapsing scenery wall. The troupe scattered, but the actor survived with evidence of a planned civilian roundup. The magician later joined XCOM, trading applause for gunfire and learning that the most important trick is getting everyone out alive.

Rain hammered the stadium roof as the grounds crew member crawled beneath the field to repair a drainage pump. Behind a maintenance wall, they found a sealed ADVENT bunker packed with confiscated civilian belongings—and a list of people scheduled for disappearance. They copied the list onto their work gloves and slipped out during a power failure. By dawn, resistance cells were evacuating the targeted families. The grounds crew member never made it back to the stadium; ADVENT had their face on every checkpoint screen.

For years, this soldier repaired musical instruments in a cramped workshop, refusing to perform at ADVENT ceremonies. One day, a damaged alien device arrived disguised inside a concertina. Its strange vibrations triggered vivid memories in anyone nearby—including memories that weren't theirs. Before ADVENT agents could reclaim it, the repairer dismantled the device and hid its components among ordinary tools. A resistance scientist helped them escape the city. Now they carry a battered tuning fork into battle, convinced the aliens have been hiding something inside the human mind.

The avalanche buried the expedition before anyone could call for help. Trapped beneath the snow, the mountain guide heard voices through a radio that had no battery. Following them through a narrow ice fissure, they emerged beside an ADVENT listening post buried inside the glacier. Its operators were tracking resistance movements through seismic sensors. The guide destroyed the equipment with a stolen explosive charge and led two surviving climbers to safety. Now they navigate XCOM through hostile terrain, trusting the mountain’s warnings more than any instrument.

The last shipment of seeds arrived with no labels, no paperwork, and a guard detail. A former seed-bank curator noticed the grains changed color under ultraviolet light. Testing one revealed alien genetic material designed to survive in human crops and spread unnoticed. Rather than destroy the collection, they smuggled samples to a resistance botanist and burned the facility’s records. ADVENT arrested their colleagues, but the curator escaped with a handful of unaltered seeds. They joined XCOM to protect what remains of Earth’s natural life—and keep the next harvest from becoming a weapon.

Nobody at the museum noticed the night watchman changing the exhibits. Over several months, ancient weapons vanished and were replaced with convincing replicas. The guard was actually hiding artifacts confiscated from families by ADVENT, returning them through an underground network. Their final delivery contained a relic with an alien tracking device embedded inside. When soldiers stormed the museum, the watchman used the building’s security shutters to trap them long enough to escape. The resistance recruited them for their patience, sharp observation, and talent for moving valuable objects under enemy surveillance.

At seventeen, this soldier won a national championship in competitive yo-yo, then spent years performing at public events to keep their family fed. During an ADVENT recruitment rally, they noticed the security team moving in precise patterns around an unmarked van. A tossed yo-yo snagged a loose cable, exposing a hidden camera network monitoring the crowd. They escaped the ensuing crackdown and passed the recordings to the resistance. Their unusual coordination and steady nerves eventually earned them a place with XCOM, where improvisation matters more than appearances.

The storm knocked out every signal buoy along the coast, leaving a cargo vessel drifting toward the rocks. A former marine cartographer launched a rescue boat and discovered the ship was carrying undocumented ADVENT prisoners. Rather than follow orders to return them to port, they navigated through a minefield using old paper charts and brought the survivors to a hidden cove. The rescued prisoners revealed a secret coastal supply route. Now the cartographer serves XCOM, carrying those same charts and refusing to let the sea become another border the aliens control.

The first clue was a chessboard with one piece missing. A former tournament arbiter noticed the same unusual arrangement appearing in confiscated apartments across three districts. Each board marked a safehouse compromised by ADVENT informants. They traced the pattern to a clerk inside the occupation’s intelligence bureau, then exposed the network before their own address appeared on the list. With nowhere left to hide, they joined the resistance. Now they approach every operation like an unfinished game, searching for the move the enemy believes nobody will see.

The radio operator heard a child singing through a channel reserved for ADVENT military traffic. Curious, they traced the signal to an abandoned weather station and found a group of runaway children using its old transmitter. One child carried a stolen data wafer containing patrol schedules. When ADVENT tracked the signal, the operator held the station long enough for everyone to escape, then fled through the storm drains. The resistance welcomed them, and XCOM gained someone who can turn obsolete equipment and a little ingenuity into a lifeline.

Nobody expected the town’s clockmaker to steal an ADVENT officer’s wristwatch. But its mechanism contained a miniature transmitter, ticking out coordinates to a hidden relay. The clockmaker dismantled it, traced the signal, and discovered a surveillance network disguised as public timekeeping devices. They replaced the transmitters with harmless decoys, giving resistance couriers several weeks of freedom before the deception was noticed. When ADVENT raided the workshop, the clockmaker escaped through a maintenance hatch, carrying tools that would later help XCOM disable alien technology.

The courtroom fell silent when the defendant began speaking in a language nobody recognized. A former sign painter in the gallery realized it was an old regional dialect, one ADVENT’s translation systems had never learned. The testimony exposed a secret prisoner exchange, and the painter helped the witness escape through a service corridor. Soon hunted for interfering with a tribunal, they vanished into the countryside. The resistance later recruited them to decipher neglected archives and forge convincing signs, turning forgotten words into weapons against the occupation.

When the power failed at the aquarium, every tank opened except one. A former marine mammal trainer found an alien organism inside, mimicking the calls of missing dolphins. The creature reacted to nearby human voices, repeating fragments of conversations recorded across the city. Before ADVENT scientists arrived, the trainer flooded the exhibit and escaped with a recording of the organism’s signals. The resistance suspected it was part of a surveillance system. XCOM recruited the trainer to help identify how the aliens listen, learn, and anticipate human behavior.

The bridge collapsed during the evacuation, leaving dozens stranded on the wrong side of the river. A former competitive lumberjack commandeered a logging crane and began lowering timber across the gap, building a makeshift crossing while ADVENT patrols closed in. When the structure finally held, they stayed behind to cut the cables and prevent enemy vehicles from following. The survivors reached safety, but the lumberjack was forced into hiding. XCOM later recruited them for their strength, mechanical instincts, and willingness to hold a position when everyone else retreats.

For three months, a rural midwife noticed that newborns in ADVENT clinics were being quietly transferred to facilities without public records. When one frightened nurse slipped her a list of destinations, she discovered the infants were being screened for unusual genetic traits. She hid the records inside a shipment of blankets and helped several families flee before the next transfer. ADVENT branded her a kidnapper. The resistance sheltered her, and she now fights to ensure no child disappears into the occupation’s laboratories again.

The first time the museum’s dinosaur skeleton moved, the night guard blamed the faulty lights. Then it turned its skull toward a locked storage room. A former paleontology preparator investigating the incident discovered ADVENT had hidden a living alien specimen inside a reconstructed fossil display, using the museum as an unmonitored containment site. They released it during a power outage and escaped amid the chaos. Though the creature vanished into the city, XCOM recruited the preparator to help identify alien biology concealed beneath familiar appearances.

A traveling puppeteer arrived in a village where nobody remembered the previous week. While performing, they noticed children repeating identical phrases whenever an ADVENT patrol passed. Suspecting something more than fear, they followed the patrol to a mobile broadcast van emitting low-frequency pulses. They stole its control unit and shut it down, restoring the villagers’ memories in fragments. With ADVENT searching for the saboteur, the puppeteer fled and eventually joined the resistance, determined to uncover how deeply the occupation had learned to manipulate human minds.

Nobody noticed the freight elevator stopping at a floor that didn’t exist. A former industrial safety inspector found the anomaly while investigating unexplained power surges at an ADVENT factory. Behind the false floor lay a workshop where alien engineers were modifying captured human equipment into tracking devices. The inspector sabotaged the lift, trapped the technicians below, and escaped with their blueprints. Though they had never fired a weapon before, they joined XCOM to put their knowledge of industrial systems to use against the machines now hunting humanity.

At dawn, the town’s pigeons began falling from the sky. A former wildlife disease researcher found microscopic transmitters embedded beneath their feathers, broadcasting signals from ADVENT’s hidden surveillance grid. Rather than alert authorities, they tracked the birds’ flight paths to a rooftop relay and dismantled it using scavenged tools. The resulting blackout let a resistance convoy cross the city undetected. ADVENT seized their laboratory, but they escaped with their field notes and joined XCOM, determined to uncover what else the aliens had taught Earth’s wildlife to do.

The first clue was a shipment of thousands of identical shoes, all sized for feet that didn’t exist. A former footwear last-maker discovered ADVENT was using the factory to disguise components for experimental prosthetics fitted to abducted civilians. They hid a tiny transmitter inside a finished boot, allowing the resistance to locate the secret workshop. When soldiers raided the factory, the maker escaped through the loading bay with its production plans. They joined XCOM not as a fighter, but as someone who knows how to turn an ordinary object into an unexpected advantage.

The storm had passed, but the lighthouse beam kept turning inland. Its keeper discovered an ADVENT device had hijacked the lamp, using coded flashes to coordinate troop movements across the countryside. Instead of destroying it, they changed the sequence to send patrols chasing phantom threats for weeks. When the deception was uncovered, the keeper escaped by boat with the original signal logs. The resistance used the logs to map enemy movements, and XCOM gained a specialist who could misdirect an entire squad without firing a shot.

The village orchestra was ordered to perform at an ADVENT memorial, but the percussionist noticed the music matched a sequence used by nearby security drones. A former instrument tuner, they altered the rhythm during rehearsal and watched the drones drift into a maintenance loop. Using the brief opening, villagers escaped through the checkpoint. The trick worked only once; ADVENT arrested the conductor and burned the instruments. The tuner fled with a pocket metronome and joined XCOM, determined to turn the enemy’s reliance on patterns into a weakness.

A sinkhole opened beneath the town square, swallowing a food truck and exposing a chamber of unfamiliar machinery. A former sewer surveyor descended to find the missing driver and discovered ADVENT had built a covert waste-disposal system for failed experiments. Something inside had survived and was clawing through the tunnels. They freed the driver, sealed the chamber with a controlled collapse, and escaped moments before security arrived. The resistance took them in, and XCOM gained someone who knows how to move through the forgotten spaces beneath occupied cities.

The wedding ended when the bride recognized an ADVENT officer among the guests as the man who had ordered her brother’s disappearance. A former professional wedding photographer, this soldier captured the officer’s face beside a concealed prisoner manifest reflected in a window. They spent the night developing the film in a makeshift darkroom while patrols searched the streets. The photographs helped resistance fighters locate a detention convoy. With their studio seized, they traded the camera for a rifle and never stopped documenting the occupation’s crimes.

For years, a competitive pastry chef perfected elaborate sugar sculptures for elite ADVENT banquets. During one event, a kitchen fire exposed a hidden shipment of alien compounds stored beneath the pantry. Realizing the ingredients were being added to civilian food supplies, the chef switched the labels, spoiled the shipment, and slipped out with a sample. ADVENT sealed every bakery in the district, but the chef escaped through a flour delivery truck. The resistance now relies on their steady hands and surprising talent for improvisation under pressure.

The museum’s new exhibit was supposed to celebrate humanity’s “peaceful partnership” with the Elders. A former conservator noticed the artifacts were still warm, though they had supposedly been excavated centuries ago. One contained a living memory imprint showing the site had been built only months earlier. They stole the imprint and exposed the exhibit as fabricated propaganda, sparking a riot that let dozens of prisoners escape nearby. With ADVENT hunting them, they joined XCOM to uncover the history the invaders are manufacturing—and the truth buried beneath it.

A power outage stranded hundreds inside an underground shopping complex, and the emergency doors refused to open. A former escape-room designer recognized the control panel’s logic as a puzzle built around false choices. While panicked crowds searched for exits, they rewired the system and unlocked a forgotten service passage. Beyond it lay an ADVENT monitoring room tracking civilian reactions to engineered crises. They copied the data before fleeing and later joined XCOM, determined to turn the aliens’ psychological games against them.

The radio station kept broadcasting after its staff vanished. A former vinyl record cutter broke in to investigate and found the transmitter running on a loop of emergency calls from future dates. One recording described an ADVENT raid that had not yet happened. They warned the targeted settlement, saving dozens, but the prediction came true elsewhere that same night. Convinced the signal was part of an alien forecasting system, they joined XCOM carrying the original recordings—and a growing fear of what the next message might reveal.

A city’s stray cats began gathering outside a condemned apartment block, refusing to leave even when ADVENT patrols approached. A former veterinary anesthetist followed them inside and discovered a hidden shelter where fugitives were being kept for illegal neural experiments. They used stolen sedatives to incapacitate the guards and guide the prisoners out through a laundry chute. Though the escape succeeded, the shelter was destroyed before investigators arrived. The anesthetist joined XCOM with a steady hand, a cool head, and no patience for anyone who treats living beings as disposable material.

During a routine rehearsal, the orchestra’s timpanist felt a second heartbeat vibrating beneath the stage. A former structural acoustician, they traced it to an ADVENT resonance device buried under the concert hall, pulsing signals that made nearby civilians unusually compliant. They sabotaged it during the opening performance, plunging the building into chaos and allowing the audience to escape. The device’s core survived, and the resistance smuggled it to XCOM for study. Now they help identify alien signals that hide beneath sounds everyone else ignores.
